limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The optimal exponent remains between \((n+1)p\) and \(3np\). The linear upper bound uses subnormality; under Kittaneh’s weaker range-inclusion hypotheses only the cube-root ideal refinement is obtained. Older commutant-modulo-ideal, subnormal-operator, and symmetric-ideal literature may contain an equivalent interpolation sharpening under different notation.
provenance: Kittaneh’s consecutive-power intertwining theorem is sharpened by normal-extension interpolation for subnormal operators, Douglas factorization, and the cubic identity for the first intertwining defect. A root-of-unity diagonal construction supplies a linear-order lower barrier.
record_title: Linear Schatten exponent for consecutive-power intertwinings
